newsitem.title: UK: UAT says wins Pilot control.
newsitem.headline: UAT says wins Pilot control.

text.p: Undervalued Assets Trust Plc said on Monday it had won control of Pilot Investment Trust, and would replace Rutherford Asset Management as Pilot's investment manager.

In a statement, it said it had received acceptances representing 51.61 percent of Pilot's shares, and 42.35 percent of warrants by 1500 on March 7, and had declared the offers unconditional. The offers would remain open until further notice.
It said it would replace Rutherford with its own investment manager, Scottish Value Management Ltd.
"The proposals put forward by Pilot's independent directors did not, in our view, offer a credible alternative to UAT's offers," said John Kay, chairman of UAT.

"This view is supported by the level of acceptances which we have received to date and it is clear that Pilot's shareholders prefer the opportunity offered by an investment in a trust with a superior performance."
Pilot said on Monday its independent directors still felt UAT's offer undervalued the company. It said UAT had requested a meeting with them as soon as possible.
Until then, the independent directors continued to recommend to shareholders and warrantholders not to accept the offer.
Pilot last week proposed a resolution to keep it as an investment trust. If this was defeated it would put forward two other resolutions.

One would seek to reconstitute Pilot as a successor trust with the same investment policy after offering those that wished to take it a cash exit. The other would reconstitute Pilot as an open-ended investment company with the same investment policy.
If all these were defeated, it would propose to liquidate Pilot.
UAT said the proposals were unsuitable.

"A successor investment trust with the same investment policy would have offered Pilot shareholders more of the same while an open-ended vehicle is, in the view of the UAT Directors, unsuited to a small companies investment portfolio in which many of the investments are relatively illiquid."
UAT said the value of its offer had risen since the original offer to 47.9 million sterling from 44.4 million due to a rise in its share price to 161.5 pence by March 6 from 158.5 on February 14.
It said it planned to seek a special dividend equal to Pilot's accrued net revenue for its current financial year.
Because it was now controlling shareholder, UAT said it did not plan to seek shareholder approval for its proposals.
